rules.title: Nonpayment eviction bar when tenant pays landlord-owed utilities
rules.requirement: A tenant may not be evicted for nonpayment of rent if the tenant used the unpaid rent to keep utility services going after notice that they were in danger of being discontinued, and the landlord was responsible for those utilities and did not pay. That money counts as part of the rent.
rules.coverage_text: Tenants whose landlord was responsible for paying electric, gas, water or sewer service.
rules.quoted_span: Note: A tenant may not be evicted for nonpayment of rent, if the tenant used the unpaid portion of rent to continue utility services to the rental premises after receiving notice that the services were in danger of being discontinued, and if the landlord was responsible for the payment of those utility services and did not make the payments required to retain the us e of those services.

rules.title: Eviction for disorderly conduct
rules.requirement: The landlord may sue for eviction if the tenant continues disorderly conduct that destroys the peace and quiet of other tenants after a written Notice to Cease. A Notice to Quit must be served at least three days before filing.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit at least three days prior to filing
rules.quoted_span: If after given written Notice to Cease disorderly conduct, the tenant continues the disorderly conduct and that conduct destroys the peace and quiet of the other tenants living in the building or neighborhood, the landlord may file a suite for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least three days prior to filing a suit for eviction (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(b)).

rules.title: Eviction for damage or destruction to the property
rules.requirement: A tenant may be evicted for intentionally or through gross negligence causing or allowing destruction, damage or injury to the property. A Notice to Quit must be served at least three days before filing.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit at least three days prior to filing
rules.quoted_span: The tenant may be evicted if they have intentionally or by reason of gross negligence caused or allowed destruction, damage, or injury to the property.

rules.title: Eviction for substantial violation of landlord's rules and regulations
rules.requirement: If the tenant continues to substantially violate reasonable rules in the lease or accepted in writing after a written Notice to Cease, the landlord may sue for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served at least one month before filing, and notices must be given on or before the start of a new month.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit at least one month prior to filing
rules.quoted_span: A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least one month prior to filing the suit for eviction. In addition, any notices must be given on or before the start of a new month (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(d)).

rules.title: Eviction for breach of lease covenants or agreements
rules.requirement: If the tenant continues to substantially breach reasonable lease covenants after a written Notice to Cease and the lease reserves a right of re-entry, the landlord may sue for eviction after a Notice to Quit served at least one month before filing. In public housing, breaches of covenants on illegal drug use or other illegal activities allow eviction without a Notice to Cease, with the Notice to Quit served per federal regulations.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit at least one month prior to filing
rules.coverage_text: Tenants whose lease reserves a right of re-entry; separate rule for public housing tenants.
rules.quoted_span: If the tenant continues to substantially violate or breach the reasonable covenants or agreements contained in the lease, after given written Notice to Cease violating or breaching those covenants or agreements and if the landlord has reserved a right of re-entry in the lease, the landlord may file a suit for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least one month prior to filing the suit for this type of eviction.

rules.title: Eviction for failure to pay rent increase
rules.requirement: The landlord may sue for eviction if the tenant fails to pay rent after notice of a rent increase and a Notice to Quit, but the increase must not be unconscionable and must comply with other laws and municipal ordinances including rent control. A Notice to Quit must be served at least one month before filing.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit at least one month prior to filing
rules.quoted_span: If a tenant fails to pay rent after being given notice of a rent increase and a Notice to Quit, the landlord may file a suit for eviction. The rent increase must not be unconscionable and must comply with all other laws or municipal ordinances, including rent control.
rules.interaction_text: must comply with all other laws or municipal ordinances, including rent control

rules.title: Eviction for health and safety violations or removal from rental market
rules.requirement: A tenant may be evicted when the landlord must board up or demolish due to cited violations, cannot abate violations with the tenant in place, must correct an illegal occupancy, or a government agency is permanently removing the property from the rental market. A Notice to Quit must be served at least three months before filing, and the tenant cannot be evicted until relocation assistance is provided.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit at least three months before filing
rules.quoted_span: A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least three months before filing a suit for eviction. The tenant can’t be evicted until relocation assistance is provided.

rules.title: Relocation assistance for illegal occupancy evictions
rules.requirement: A tenant evicted to correct an illegal occupancy is entitled to relocation assistance equal to six times the tenant's monthly rent, paid by the landlord. If not paid at least five days before removal, the tenant may be paid from a municipal revolving relocation assistance fund, which the landlord must repay.
rules.key_value: six times the tenant’s monthly rent
rules.coverage_text: Tenants evicted under the illegal occupancy cause (G 3).
rules.penalty: If the municipality has no relocation fund and the landlord does not pay on time, interest accrues at 18% per year until paid in full; the amount due is a lien on the property that the tenant may enforce by filing a lien statement.
rules.quoted_span: Any tenant evicted under G 3) (illegal occupancy) is entitled to relocation assistance in an amount equal to six times the tenant’s monthly rent.

rules.title: Eviction to permanently retire property from residential use
rules.requirement: A landlord permanently retiring a building or mobile home park from residential use may sue for eviction after serving a Notice to Quit at least 18 months before filing. No legal action may be taken until the lease expires.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit at least 18 months prior to filing
rules.coverage_text: Buildings or mobile home parks being permanently retired from residential use, where the circumstances in section (G) do not apply.
rules.quoted_span: If the landlord wants to permanently retire a building or mobile home park from residential use, provided the circumstances covered under section (G) above do not apply, the landlord may file suit for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least 18 months prior to filing the suit for eviction.

rules.title: Eviction for refusal to accept reasonable lease changes
rules.requirement: When the lease expires, if the tenant refuses after written notice to accept reasonable but substantial changes, the landlord may sue and the court decides if the changes are reasonable. A Notice to Quit must be served at least one month before filing.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit at least one month before filing
rules.quoted_span: If after written notice the tenant refuses to accept those changes the landlord may file a suit for eviction and the court will determine if the proposed changes are reasonable.

rules.title: Eviction for continuous nonpayment or habitual late payment
rules.requirement: If the tenant continuously fails to pay rent or habitually pays late after a written Notice to Cease, the landlord may sue for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served at least one month before filing.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit at least one month before filing
rules.quoted_span: If the tenant continuously fails to pay rent or habitually pays late, after written Notice to Cease, the landlord may file a suit for eviction. A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least one month before filing a suit for eviction (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(j)).

rules.title: Eviction for conversion to condominium, cooperative or fee simple ownership
rules.requirement: A landlord converting a building or mobile home park to condominium, cooperative or fee simple ownership may sue for eviction after complying with conversion regulations and serving a Notice to Quit at least three years before filing; no action until the lease expires. Courts grant up to five one-year stays if comparable housing was not offered, and no action may be brought against protected senior citizen or disabled tenants.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit at least three years before filing
rules.coverage_text: Buildings or mobile home parks being converted to condominium, cooperative, or fee simple ownership of two or more dwelling units or park sites.
rules.exemptions: Senior citizen or disabled tenants with protected tenancy status under the Senior Citizens and Disabled Protected Tenancy Act of 1992.
rules.quoted_span: A Notice to Quit must be ser ved on the tenant at least three years before filing a suit for eviction. No legal action may be taken until the lease expires (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(k)).
rules.interaction_text: No action for possession shall be brought against a senior citizen tenant or disabled tenant with protected tenancy status pursuant to the “Senior Citizens and Disabled Protected Tenancy Act of 1992,”

rules.title: Eviction for owner occupancy or sale to occupying buyer
rules.requirement: Owners of converted condo/co-op units (for tenancies starting after recording), owners of three or less condominium or cooperative units, and owners of buildings with three residential units or less may evict to personally occupy the unit or sell it vacant to a buyer who will occupy it. A Notice to Quit must be served at least two months before filing, and no action until the lease expires.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit at least two months prior to filing
rules.coverage_text: Converted condominium/cooperative units with tenancies beginning after recording; owners of three or fewer condo or co-op units; buildings with three residential units or less.
rules.quoted_span: The landlord may file for eviction, if the owner of a building with three residential units or less seeks to personally occupy a unit, or has contracted to sell the residential unit to a buyer who wishes to personally occupy it and the contract fo r sale calls for the unit to be vacant at the time of closing. A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least two months prior to filing suit for eviction.

rules.title: Eviction upon termination of employment-based tenancy
rules.requirement: If a tenant occupies the property on condition of employment by the landlord and that employment ends, the landlord may sue for eviction after serving a Notice to Quit three days before filing.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit three days prior to filing
rules.coverage_text: Tenants residing on condition of employment by the landlord, such as a superintendent or janitor.
rules.quoted_span: A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant three days prior to filing a suit for eviction (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(m)).

rules.title: Eviction for drug offense committed on the property
rules.requirement: The landlord may sue for eviction if the tenant was convicted of or pleaded guilty to drug offenses on the property and has not completed or is not participating in a drug rehabilitation program, or lets such a person occupy the premises. No suit more than two years after the delinquency finding, conviction or release, whichever is later; Notice to Quit at least three days before filing.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit at least three days prior to filing
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to a tenant allowing a juvenile to reside at the property where the juvenile has been found delinquent due to use or possession of drugs.
rules.quoted_span: No eviction suit may be brought more than two years after : the juvenile was found to be delinquent; conviction of the person; of after the person’s release from incarceration , whichever is later. A Notice to Quit must be served on the tenant at least three days prior to filing suit for eviction (N.J.S.A. 2A:18-61.1(n)).

rules.title: Eviction for assault or threats against the landlord, family or employees
rules.requirement: The landlord may sue for eviction if the tenant was convicted of, pleaded guilty to, or as a juvenile was found delinquent for assault or terrorist threats against the landlord, the landlord's family or employee, or knowingly lets such a person reside there. No suit more than two years after the later of the finding, conviction or release; Notice to Quit at least three days before filing.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit at least three days prior to filing
rules.quoted_span: The landlord may file for eviction, if the tenant has been convicted of or pleaded guilty to, or if a juvenile has been found by the court to be delinquent due to an offense involving assault or terrorist threats against the landlord, a member of the landl ord’s family or an employee of the landlord.

rules.title: Eviction after civil liability for criminal activities
rules.requirement: The landlord may sue for eviction if a civil court finds the tenant liable for theft of property on the premises, assaults or terrorist threats against the landlord, family or employee, or illegal drug activity on the premises without rehabilitation, or if the tenant knowingly lets such a person reside there. No suit more than two years after the later of the finding, conviction or release; Notice to Quit at least three days before filing.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit at least three days prior to filing
rules.exemptions: Does not apply to a tenant allowing a juvenile to reside at the property where the juvenile has been found delinquent due to the use or possession of drugs.
rules.quoted_span: The landlord may file for eviction, if the tenant is found by a civil court proceeding (not criminal) to be liable fo r involvement in theft of property located on the premises, involvement in assaults or terrorist threats against the landlord, a member of the landlord’s family or an employee of the landlord, or involved in illegal drug activities that takes place on the premises and that tenant has not in connection with his sentence for the drug offense either (1) successfully completed or (2) been admitted to and continues during probation participation towards completion of a drug rehabilitation program.

rules.title: Eviction for conviction for theft of property
rules.requirement: The landlord may sue for eviction if the tenant was convicted of, pleaded guilty to, or as a juvenile was found delinquent for theft of property from the landlord or other tenants in the same building or complex, or knowingly lets such a person reside there. A Notice to Quit must be served at least three days before filing.
rules.key_value: Notice to Quit at least three days prior to filing
rules.quoted_span: The landlord may file for eviction, if the tenant has been convicted of or pleaded guilty to, or if a juvenile has been found to be delinquent by the Court due to an offense involving theft of property from the landlord or from tenants residing in the same building or complex.

rules.title: Eviction for human trafficking
rules.requirement: The landlord may sue for eviction if a civil action finds the tenant committed human trafficking on the premises, building, complex or mobile home park, or knowingly harbored or let a person engaged in human trafficking occupy the premises. No action may be brought more than two years after the violation ended.
rules.quoted_span: The landlord may file for eviction, if the tenant in a civil action is found to have committed a violation of the human trafficking provisions set forth in section 1 of P.L. 2005, c.77 (2C:13-8) within or upon the leased premises , building, or complex of the building and land appurtenant thereto, or the mobile home park, in which those premises are located, or, being the tenant or lessee of such leased premises, knowingly harbors or harbored a person engaged in human trafficking, or permits or permitted such a person to occupy those premises for residential purposes, whether continuously or intermittently.

rules.title: Evictions for owner-occupied two- and three-family dwellings
rules.requirement: Tenants of landlord-occupied two- and three-family dwellings can be removed only by court order, on proof of listed causes such as holdover, nonpayment, disorderly conduct, damage, rule violations or lease breaches with right of re-entry. A three-month notice to quit applies to at-will or year-to-year tenancies, one month for month-to-month and other tenancies, three days for disorderly, destructive or rule/lease violations, and no further notice for nonpayment.
rules.key_value: three (3) month notice for at will or year-to-year tenancy; one (1) month notice for month-to-month
rules.quoted_span: Tenants of landlord-occupied two- and three-family dwellings can be removed only when a court issues an order for eviction.

rules.title: Rooming and boarding house evictions
rules.requirement: Owners of rooming and boarding houses must follow the good causes and notice requirements of the Eviction Law when evicting residents, unless otherwise ordered by the Bureau. They must also give at least three working days' notice to the County Welfare Board before starting an eviction action.
rules.key_value: at least three (3) working days’ notice to the County Welfare Board
rules.coverage_text: Rooming and boarding houses, i.e. buildings with at least two living units occupied by unrelated persons without private kitchens and bathrooms, unless an exception in the Rooming and Boarding House Act applies.
rules.exemptions: Except if otherwise ordered by the Bureau of Rooming and Boarding House Standards.
rules.quoted_span: There is a further requirement that the owner give at least three (3) working days’ notice to the County Welfare Board before starting the eviction action for any resident (N.J.A.C. 5:26-3.4(c)).
rules.interaction_text: require owners of rooming and boarding houses to follow the good causes and notice requirements of the Eviction Law when evicting residents, except if otherwise ordered by the Bureau
